agent_notes: 21:4 says 'as God commanded him'; the command of the eighth day is 17:12.

17:19, 21 promise Isaac 'at this time next year' and the chapter says 'at the set time of which God had spoken' (21:2): FULFILLS_PROPHECY from gen_17. The 18:10 repetition (gen_18.son_promised_to_sarah) is a second cause I also link.

'At that time' (21:22) is ambiguous: Rashbam says at Isaac's birth, Radak at the birth or the weaning. Revised after review: I first anchored it on the rescue's end with a 1-year margin, which excluded the birth reading. Now it is anchored on the birth with offset 1 year and margin 18 months, so the span covers both the birth (Rashbam) and the weaning (Radak). The text order would put it after the rescue, but 'at that time' is not a sequence marker, so the timeline may show it before the weaning feast. The place of the talks is not stated; Abraham is at Beer-sheba by 21:31–32 (Beer-sheba to Philistia, about 54 km straight line; the return of Abimelech and Phicol is not given its own event).

history.note: [should_fix] Widen the margin so it covers both readings, birth and weaning: for example keep the anchor and set the margin to 2 years, or anchor on evt.gen_21.sarah_bears_isaac START with an offset of about 1 year and a margin of about 1.5 years. Say in the temporal note that the span runs from the birth to the weaning. (GEN.21.22: "וַיְהִי בָּעֵת הַהִוא" ("and it came to pass at that time"); Rashbam ad loc.: "שנולד יצחק"; Radak ad loc.: "בָּעֵת שֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק אוֹ שֶׁנִּגְמַל".)

[consider] Raise the margin to 7 days, or drop the circumcision alternative from the note. (GEN.21.3–4: the naming is told before the circumcision "בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַת יָמִים" with no time word of its own.)

agent_notes: 'Many days' (21:34) is a MACRO_ERA span. Rashi counts 26 years in Philistia (after 25 years at Hebron, ending 12 years before the binding), which I take as the duration with a margin of 10 years. I anchor it on the start of the move to Gerar (Gen 20:1, c. 2067 BCE) and let it run 26 years. Radak reads the many days as the rest of Abraham's residence in the Negev. The sojourn overlaps the earlier events of the chapter by design.

history.note: [consider] Either give the speech a time_of_day of night (LAYLAH) if you mean a night vision, or drop 'the night before' from the note and say it falls between the demand and the next morning. (GEN.21.14: "וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר" ("Abraham rose early in the morning") is the only time word; 21:12 has none.)

[consider] Use the tier the chapter uses for scenes with no time word of their own, and keep the estimate in the note. (GEN.21.15: "וַיִּכְלוּ הַמַּיִם מִן־הַחֵמֶת" ("the water was spent in the skin"), with no time word.)

agent_notes: Weaning age is not stated. Offset 2 years with margin 1 year: a nursing span of about two years is the usual ancient reading (cf. 1 Sam 1:22–24, which Rashbam cites on 21:8; 2 Macc 7:27 says three). Alternatives of 3 or 5 years would still fall inside the margin to a degree. Ishmael would then be about 16 (born when Abraham was 86, 16:16), which fits 'mocking' (21:9) but is old for being carried (21:14, 'placing it on her shoulder, and the boy'); this is a known tension, not resolved here.

21:20–21 compresses Ishmael's boyhood and marriage. I give it a 10-year duration from the rescue with a 5-year margin; the text offers no figure, so MACRO_ERA. The marriage itself (21:21) is not a separate event because nothing dates it.

Dated by Abraham's age (100, 21:5), through anchor.isaac_birth, offset 0, margin 1 year because an age covers the whole year. Gen 20 events sit at 2067 BCE (Abraham 99); the birth follows in the next year, as 18:10 'at this time next year' says. The conception (9 months earlier) is not a separate event.

Text does not date Sarah's sight of Ishmael 'mocking'; the tradition and the sequence place it at the feast of 21:8. I put it a few hours into the feast day, with a margin of a week to cover a later day.

notes.note: Every verse 21:1–34 is covered. 21:5 (Abraham's age, a narrator's aside) sits inside the circumcision event, which it follows. 21:34 ('many days') is its own long event.

Divine speeches checked: 21:1 (word to Sarah, fulfilled in 21:2); 21:12 (Isaac as seed; 'listen to Sarah'; fulfilled by the sending in 21:14, linked as TRIGGERS, not as prophecy); 21:13 and 21:18 ('I will make him a nation', 'a great nation') are not shown fulfilled in this chapter: 25:12–18 (Ishmael's twelve princes) will fulfil them, and that chapter's session should write the link from evt.gen_21.god_reassures_abraham and evt.gen_21.angel_rescues_hagar_and_ishmael. 21:17 'God heard the boy's voice' leads to the rescue (TRIGGERS).

Considered and dropped: a link from gen_20.abraham_prays_and_god_heals to the birth (Pseudo-Jonathan on 21:1 ties the visitation to Abraham's prayer for Abimelech). 20:17–18 says the wombs of Abimelech's house were closed and then healed; 21:1 does not say the prayer caused Sarah's conception, so I left it as a note.
